_comment: Which game viewers this application serves, and the release each comes from.
A cartridge publishes its build output as a GitHub release -- one archive, laid out as its
dist/ -- so the coordinate is a repository and nothing outside this directory is read. The
latest release is taken unless the variable named by `env` names a tag, or a directory laid
The Dockerfile fetches each release in a pair of stages, because a Dockerfile cannot loop; a
second game is an entry here AND those stages there. scripts/vendor-viewers.sh reads this file alone.
`engines` IS EVERY RELEASE THE LADDER HAS EVER PLAYED, and it only ever grows. A replay is
re-simulated from its actions, so it is drawn by the viewer of the engine that played it, which
the image keeps by digest beside the current one; a match on an engine missing from this list
is refused rather than drawn by another. A release the ladder plays goes in here BEFORE the next
one is published, or its matches stop drawing the day it stops being the latest.
